newsitem.title: USA: NYC loses $13 mln in property tax scheme.
newsitem.headline: NYC loses $13 mln in property tax scheme.

text.p: New York City's Department of Investigation said Thursday 29 people were charged in a bribery scheme that cost the city $13 million in property taxes.
DOI said it hopes to recoup the tax losses along with $7 million in interest from the defendants.

Among those charged were three employees of New York City Department of Finance, including the former director of the Brooklyn City Collector's Office and 26 property owners and their representatives. The scheme allegedly began in 1992.

According to the charges, which are filed in Manhattan and Brooklyn federal courts, the city employees allegedly took bribes to reduce or eliminate property taxes and interest on some 1,600 properties.

The complaints allege that over the last six months alone, more than $250,000 in cash and other valuable items including late-model luxury cars were used to bribe city employees to eliminate more than $2 million in unpaid real property taxes and interest.

In some cases, the employees manipulated computer records to show that taxes had been paid when they had not been paid. In other instances, legitimate taxpayers' payments were misapplied to the accounts of bribe-paying property owners.
Other methods used in the scheme involved arranging to credit property owners with checks that the employees knew would be dishonored.

The investigation began in late 1994 when the Department of Finance learned of suspicious transactions taking place between certain DOF employees and landlords. Federal authorities joined in the probe in 1995.
